research_rationale:
Identity: the registered original is the Federal Register printing of Executive Order 10157 at 15 FR 5834 (govinfo text layer, grade original_representation_unverified), signed August 28, 1950; the source URL is the govinfo PDF of the August 30, 1950 issue. The register title is Enabling Certain Employees of the Federal Government To Acquire a Competitive Status.  Inventory corrected: one clause, offsets 3563 to 5979 of the held text, from the enacting words through paragraph 4. The dossier lists ten clauses, including entries with duplicate-style names (a-dup2, c-dup2, c-3, c-4) whose offsets lie within paragraphs 2 to 4; the single clause below covers paragraphs 1 to 4 once. Content: paragraph 1 gives any employee without competitive status who on the date of the order is serving in an active-duty status in a competitive-service position a competitive status on meeting four conditions (continuous service for two years, an efficiency rating or certification, agency recommendation within six months, and a noncompetitive examination); paragraph 2 excludes postmasters, certain rural carriers and certain non-preference persons; paragraph 3 treats employees on active military duty as in active-duty status; paragraph 4 directs the Civil Service Commission to issue regulations. Ending: Executive Order 12553 of February 25, 1986 (51 FR 7237, held govinfo text layer) has an enacting sentence reading, in part, "it is hereby ordered that the following Executive Orders, and" and, on the next line, "any amendments thereto, are revoked:" (the table row for 10157 describes authorizing certain Government employees to acquire a competitive civil service status). The enacting sentence has no effective-date wording and no exception or saving clause, so the first end is dated on signing, 1986-02-25 (a reading disclosed for the reviewer; the March 3, 1986 printing date is not used). Later events, both strike-and-insert amendments under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 and not ends. (1) Executive Order 10217 of February 26, 1951 amends paragraph 1(c) to read that the recommendation must be made to the Civil Service Commission by the head of the agency within six months of the date of the order, with a proviso extending the period, for an employee who left or leaves his civilian position to enter the armed forces, to six months after honorable termination of military service. (2) Executive Order 10288 of September 7, 1951 further amends paragraph 1(a) by adding a proviso on substitute employees in the postal service appointed on or before August 28, 1948, and amends paragraph 1(c) again by adding a proviso that recommendations in the postal-substitute cases, and in cases of agency inadvertence, may be accepted if received by the Commission not later than March 1, 1952. Neither order has effective-date wording, so each took effect on signing. Earlier-end check: the order's own terms contain no end date or termination clause; the six-month recommendation window, as extended to March 1, 1952, is a condition on acquiring status and is not an end of the order. Executive Order 10535 of June 9, 1954 (held text) authorizes the Civil Service Commission to confer competitive status on persons who met the requirements of this order, "as amended", but were not recommended through administrative error; it recites this order as still in effect and does not revoke or supersede it, so it is context and not an end. The dossier chain names Executive Orders 10217, 10288 and 12553. Prior research: the dossier shows no canonical prior claim and no conflicting versions. Searches: current-law:usc, current-law:ecfr and later-events:ofr_catalog, each marked complete in the packet with no coverage warning.
